Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Second Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan II) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 11: MAQABIS-OF-MOAB'S PENITENCE-RENEWAL AFTER SONS' MARTYRDOM — second deep-penitential-arc paralleling Ch 3's conversion-penance (the pit-immersion). The bereaved-father returns to sackcloth-and-ashes after his sons' martyrdom; fasts; cries-out to God. The double-penitential-arc structure (conversion-penance + bereavement-penance) parallels: 2 SAMUEL 12:15-23 (David's seven-days-of-fasting-and-prayer over his sick-son; rises and worships after the death); JOB 1:20-22 (Job's first-bereavement worship-response — 'the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away'); 1 KINGS 21:27-29 (Ahab's reluctant humility); PSALM 13 (the dark-night-of-the-soul lament). Meqabyan's distinctive feature: the SECOND-PENITENTIAL ARC DOES NOT RECANT THE CONVERSION — Maqabis-of-Moab does not blame God or return to idols; instead, his bereavement-penance DEEPENS HIS COVENANT-FAITH. The pattern parallels the EOTC spiritual-formation-tradition of progressive-deepening-through-suffering.

PENITENTIAL-PSALM CITATION at Maqabis-of-Moab's bereavement-prayer (vv. 9-15) — likely echoing PSALM 51 (the prototype-penitential-psalm — David after Bathsheba). The psalm's structure: confession-of-sin + plea-for-mercy + restoration-request + commitment-to-praise. The standard EOTC penitential-psalms (Psalms 6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143 — the seven penitential-psalms of the Christian tradition) are integrated into Tewahedo liturgy at Säʿatat (Liturgy of the Hours), and Athanasius's LETTER TO MARCELLINUS (γ.4.9.D ATTR_MARC source) is the canonical-patristic guidebook for penitential-psalm-praying-by-disposition. Meqabyan's citation here makes 2 Mq an exegetical-bridge between LXX-Maccabean-prayer-tradition (1 Macc 4:30-33 + 2 Macc 1:24-29 — the Hasmonean prayers) and the Davidic-penitential-psalm-tradition. The bereaved-king's prayer locates him in the canonical-prayer-tradition rather than as a tragic-mourning figure.
